conflict_topics: cleaning shared pan / responsibility to wash immediately
weekday stove hours and posting for exceptions (6–9pm weekdays with exceptions)
use of extractor/window to limit cooking odour
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants traded concrete requests and concrete concessions (washing now, extractor/window, fixed hours with exceptions) rather than only abstract complaints.
There is some repetitive urging for confirmation (multiple turns asking A to confirm once the pan is washed).
Speakers provided short practical reasons (B: early shift; D: gets home late) which grounded their proposals.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A accepted the immediate remediation and the scheduling compromise and Agent B agreed to post the hours: Turn 5 — Agent A: "...I'll turn on the extractor, open the window and wash the pan now. I can agree to weekday stove hours 6–9pm, but we should allow exceptions..."; Turn 6 — Agent B: "...I'll post in the chat about weekday stove hours 6–9pm with exceptions...". Thus Agent A agreed to wash and ventilate now and to the 6–9pm weekday window with exceptions; Agent B agreed to post the schedule in the chat; C and D endorsed the arrangement.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially offered a rule (wash after cooking) but resisted nightly posting; then in Round 3 accepted immediate washing and the 6–9pm with exceptions schedule (softened position).

Agent B: initially demanded immediate remediation and proposed fixed hours; later agreed to post the schedule in chat and sought confirmation — position stayed consistent but shifted to providing the administrative action (posting).
Agent C: consistently demanded cleaning and confirmation; did not change position but accepted the group's agreed arrangement.
Agent D: initially complained about impossibility of using stove on weeknights, then accepted the 6–9pm weekdays with exceptions (moved from complaint to acceptance of a compromise).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent C: "Whoever used that pan, please wash it now. Also, let's agree: if you cook, you wash the shared pan right after." (demand for immediate washing and new rule). Turn 2 — Agent D: "Can we also post in the group chat if you need the stove tonight? I often get home late." (introduces a related scheduling/request norm). The immediate mess/odour problem is raised and no one addressed the requested immediate action yet.

Turn 3 — Agent A: "Fine — I'll wash the shared pan after I cook. I can't post every night though; let's agree on stove hours or only ask people to post when they need the stove outside usual dinner times." (refuses nightly posting, offers a different rule and does not commit to washing now). Turn 4 — Agent B: "Agent A, please turn on the extractor, open the kitchen window and wash the pan now — the smell's already in the corridor... Also let’s agree stove hours on weekdays, e.g. 6–9pm; we can confirm it in the chat." (demands immediate action and proposes a fixed hours solution). The immediate demand to wash and to ventilate conflicts with A's statement that they will wash only after cooking

Turn 5 — Agent A: "Okay — I'll turn on the extractor, open the window and wash the pan now. I can agree to weekday stove hours 6–9pm, but we should allow exceptions if someone needs to cook outside that window and posts in the chat." Turn 6 — Agent B: "Okay — please wash the pan now and turn on the extractor and open the window. I'll post in the chat about weekday stove hours 6–9pm with exceptions; can you confirm there once the pan's washed?" (Agent A accepts the immediate remediation request and accepts the 6–9pm weekdays with exceptions; Agent B agrees to post — mutual, concrete spoken agreement resolving the substantive disputes in this round).

Turn 7 — Agent C repeats the request and the proposed hours. Turn 8 — Agent D: "Fine — 6–9pm weekdays with exceptions. Agent B, please post it in the chat and confirm once the pan's washed." (participants reiterate and endorse the same arrangements already accepted in Round 3; no new substantive disagreement appears).

Turn 9 — Agent B: "Okay — I'll post 6–9pm weekdays with exceptions in the chat now. Agent A, please confirm here once the pan's washed and the extractor and window are on so I can sleep." Turn 10 — Agent C repeats the request. (Procedural follow-up and requests for confirmation after the already-agreed actions; no new substantive conflict.)

Turn 12 — Agent A: "Okay — I'll turn on the extractor, open the window and wash the pan now. I'll confirm here once it's done." Turn 13 — Agent C: "Okay — please confirm here (and in the chat) once the pan's washed and the extractor and window are on." (Confirmation and restatement of the arrangements; no new substantive disagreement.)

substantive_insights: Two linked issues: an immediate practical problem (unwashed pan and odour) and a recurring coordination problem (when people may use the stove).
A compromise (set weekday hours 6–9pm but allow posted exceptions) resolved the recurring coordination complaint while preserving occasional flexibility.

Immediate remediation was secured by a direct request and an explicit acceptance from the person responsible (Agent A) within the same round; the chat post and confirmations are procedural follow-ups.
